title: Mannitol Salt Agar

references.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

purpose: Selects for Staphylococcus species using a high salt concentration that inhibits most other bacteria, and differentiates mannitol-fermenting from non-fermenting staphylococci.
targetOrganisms: Staphylococcus species, notably distinguishing Staphylococcus aureus from coagulase-negative staphylococci

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

preparationSummary: Suspend the dehydrated powder per the manufacturer's stated concentration, heat with agitation to boiling to fully dissolve, then sterilize and pour while still liquid.
storage: Refrigerate prepared plates in sealed bags, protected from light.
expectedAppearance: Pale red/pink agar (phenol red at neutral-to-slightly-alkaline pH) before inoculation.
qualityControl: Verify selectivity (a Gram-negative control should be inhibited) and differentiation (a known mannitol-fermenting Staphylococcus aureus strain should turn the medium yellow; a non-fermenting coagulase-negative staphylococcus should remain pink) against reference organisms.

reactions.reaction: Colonies surrounded by a yellow zone as fermentation acid shifts the phenol red indicator
Growth with the surrounding medium remaining pink/red
Inhibited by the high (7.5%) salt concentration

manufacturerNotes: Mannitol fermentation on MSA is a useful presumptive indicator for Staphylococcus aureus but is not by itself confirmatory — a coagulase test or equivalent is needed for definitive identification, and rare mannitol-fermenting coagulase-negative strains exist.
